proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The finite symmetric probe certificate is false already when \(K=4\) and \(\mathcal X\) is a singleton.  More precisely, for every \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\) and \(m_*\in(0,1)\), there are \(p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) with \(M(p)\ge m_*\), a number \(r_1>0\), and \(g\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\) such that \(E_{p,r}(g)=0\) for every \(0<r\le r_1\).  Nevertheless, for every \(\kappa>0\) and all sufficiently small such \(r\), there is \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\) satisfying \(\operatorname{supp}(q)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(p)\), \(\lVert q-p\rVert_\infty<\kappa r\), and \(M(q)>0\), while \(\lVert\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(q)-\Phi(p)\rVert_\infty>0\).  Consequently, no finite collection of rows with \(V(z)=\max_\nu|a_\nu^{\mathsf T}z|\) and \(V(z)\le E_{p,r}(z)\) for every \(z\) can also satisfy \(\lVert\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(q)-\Phi(p)\rVert_\infty\le V(q-p)\) for every such \(q\).  Thus the original positive assertion fails before its covariance-traction condition is reached.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original claim is false because its probe functional is even, whereas the legal inner envelope is one-sided at a binding selection-total face.  The explicit legal \(K=4\) latent table in the replacement proof has \(E_{p,r}(g)=0\) but a nonzero endpoint increment in direction \(-g\); \(V(g)=V(-g)\) then makes \(\mathrm{P1}\) and \(\mathrm{P2}\) contradictory.  A future positive result must use an oriented envelope and re-prove relative quantile transfer; adding support, gap, or variance floors would not repair this stated certificate.

proposed.justification: The explicit counterexample identifies the exact obstruction to replacing the non-even legal directional envelope by an unsigned maximum of linear probe rows.
proposed.gap: At a binding selection-total face, legality permits motion only toward a larger upper survivor margin.  The endpoint extension can move in the opposite ambient direction even though every nearby legal derivative vanishes in the forward direction.
proposed.consumer: The downstream uniform-coverage argument cannot use the symmetric probe reduction; it must instead establish an oriented legal comparison and a corresponding relative conditional-quantile theorem before the headline claim can be recovered.

prose_updates.tldr: The accepted sharp-identification theorem still supplies \(\Theta_I(p)=[L(p),U(p)]\) for the survivor-complier probability of benefit, and the separated-face oracle and width calculations are unaffected.  The proposed uniform proof, however, does not close: an explicit legal singleton-cell \(K=4\) law refutes the finite unsigned-probe lemma on which relative calibration was based.  At a binding selection-total face, \(E_{p,r}(g)=0\) in the legally inward direction, while the algebraic endpoint changes in direction \(-g\).  Because \(V(g)=\max_\nu|a_\nu^{\mathsf T}g|\) is even, it cannot satisfy both legal-envelope domination and endpoint-increment domination.  Uniform joint coverage therefore remains unproved pending an oriented, non-even legal comparison and its own relative critical-value transfer.

project_justification.fill: The current round supplies a finite latent response-type counterexample to the proposed symmetric legalization step.  It isolates the required repair: retain the orientation of one-sided legal faces, for example through positive parts of signed rows, and establish relative Gaussian quantile transfer for that non-even statistic.  No support, cut-gap, cell-mass, or variance floor is introduced.

prose_updates.related_work: The accepted CausalSmith survivor-complier benefit result supplies the exact sharp endpoint formula and full-law sharpness; identification is imported rather than reproved.  Angrist, Imbens, and Rubin (1996) support conditional instrument randomization, treatment consistency, and no defiers, while Dong and Heiler (2026) support treatment-mediated selection and outcome consistency together with covariate-specific weak selection monotonicity.  The fixed \(\epsilon\) overlap bound and fixed \(m_*\) denominator floor are uniform-class strengthenings here.  Fang and Santos (2019) and Hong and Li (2018) explain derivative-resampling methods, but their generic results do not construct the required nearby legal observed laws.  Frandsen and Pond (2025), Imai and Okamoto (2026), and Andrews and Guggenberger (2009) begin from regular or standardized representations that do not resolve the present one-sided legal-face problem.  The explicit counterexample shows that the previously proposed unsigned finite-probe reduction is unavailable; Vijaykumar's scale-free unsigned-Gaussian bound cannot repair a deterministic comparison that is already false.
prose_updates.interpretation: The proposed rectangle is aimed at simultaneous coverage of the sharp endpoint pair \(\Phi(p_n)=(L(p_n),U(p_n))\), not at redefining the causal probability \(\theta_B\).  The imported identification theorem continues to give \(\Theta_I(p_n)=[L(p_n),U(p_n)]\).  Exact common-Gaussian calibration on separated regular faces remains a distinct result, but uniform honesty on arbitrary tied and degenerating faces is not established by the refuted symmetric-probe argument.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The obstruction is deterministic and occurs with one covariate cell, \(K=4\), fixed propensity one half, positive instrument cells, positive capacity coordinates, and a positive aggregate survivor mass.  Thus zero-arm discontinuities, rare support, covariance estimation, and anti-concentration are not the source of failure.  The legal envelope is non-even at the binding selection-total face, whereas the proposed \(V_{p,r}\) is even.  A valid uniform proof must construct an oriented legal envelope and redo its lower-quantile transfer; the present analysis supplies neither that theorem nor a uniform-coverage conclusion.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Sharp identification is imported from the accepted parent and is not a contribution of this note.  The separated regular-face calibration, root-\(n\) width calculations, and diagnostic arrays are not overturned by this counterexample.  The all-array uniform joint-coverage claim remains open because its finite unsigned-probe premise is false even without vanishing cells or variances.  No individual support, survivor-cell, cut-gap, or variance floor and no deterministic guard has been added.
